meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('painful').

examples.text: Я понимаю, что эти изменения очень болезненны.
examples.trans: I understand that these changes are very painful.

examples.text: Болезненны — это когда любимая команда не может выиграть.
examples.trans: Painful is when your favorite team cannot win.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Extra money or an extra reward. Common masculine noun meaning 'bonus' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here's a bonus for you, Pasha. Invest it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.
examples.trans: Pasha, you won't win this election.

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: + dative of person. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'платить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay', paired with 'платить'.

examples.trans: I have already paid for dinner.

examples.text: И денег я тебе заплачу. В десять раз больше!
examples.trans: And I'll pay you money. Ten times more!

meanings.note: Без изменений = no change. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'менение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'change, alteration' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are changes in the timetable.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'catastrophe, disaster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for us!

examples.text: Это просто катастрофа для нашей кампании!
examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for our campaign!

examples.text: О нет, это катастрофа для кухни!
examples.trans: Oh no, this is a disaster for the kitchen!

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Radio and phone phrase. Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('large, prominent, major').

examples.trans: He dreams of becoming a major minister.
A large store opened in the city.

examples.text: Этот хряк мечтает стать крупным министром.
examples.trans: This pig dreams of becoming a major minister.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: 'менять что на что' = to swap something for something
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to change; to swap', paired with 'поменять'.

examples.trans: I'll swap an iPhone for a phone.

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: after numbers: два миллиона, пять миллионов

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Predicative or adverb. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'возможно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Как это сегодня вечером? Это невозможно!
examples.trans: What do you mean, this evening? That's impossible!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'impossible' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This is an entirely impossible situation.
It is impossible to work in such noise.
In the fish? That is impossible, Chef!

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.en: to be quiet, to keep silent for a bit
meanings.note: politer or softer than молчать in commands

examples.trans: Let's be quiet for a moment.

examples.text: Помолчите, пожалуйста. Не видите, человеку плохо?
examples.trans: Please be quiet. Can't you see someone isn't feeling well?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: By the rules. Common neuter noun meaning 'rule' in everyday Russian.
By the rules. Common neuter noun meaning 'rule' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
examples.trans: All by the rules, like a knights' tournament.

meanings.note: Это правильно = that's right. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: adverb or conjunction in 'прежде чем'
Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: The Russian currency. Common masculine noun meaning 'rouble' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'net, network' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Рыбаки на рассвете быстро вытащили полные сети на берег.
examples.trans: At dawn the fishermen quickly hauled the full nets onto the shore.

examples.text: Крупная ресторанная сеть хотела перекупить нашего лучшего шефа.
examples.trans: A large restaurant chain wanted to poach our best chef.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: + genitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

In exclamations. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.en: to observe, follow rules or regime
meanings.note: Transitive verb. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'облюдать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to observe, comply with', paired with 'соблюсти'.

examples.trans: It is important to keep quiet.

examples.text: Тогда соблюдайте режим и не нарушайте.
examples.trans: Then observe the regime and do not violate it.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.en: to hear, catch the sound of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'слышать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'слышать'.

examples.trans: I am glad to hear that.
I just want to hear the truth.

meanings.note: Participle/adjective. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'становленный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('established, set').

examples.text: Я помню все установленные законом правила.
examples.trans: I remember all the rules established by law.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Часть сделки = part of the deal. Common feminine noun meaning 'part, share; unit' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'part, share; unit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I kept my part of the deal.
This is the best part of the book.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, я выполнил свою часть сделки.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I kept my part of the deal.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: + past tense: 'чтобы свидетели были'
+ infinitive. Core Russian conj meaning 'so that, in order to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
